cards.explanation: The answer is True. The LORD tells Jeremiah, His prophet, “You must not marry or have sons or daughters in this place.” (Jeremiah 16:2) That's a lot to hear about your own life, friends. I think I'd have needed to sit down for a minute, and maybe hold on to my hat.

The answer is deadly diseases and the sword. The LORD says, “They will die from deadly diseases.” (Jeremiah 16:4) Then He adds that they will be “…finished off by sword and famine…” This part is heavy, friends, so I'll just say it plainly and let it be heavy.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “They will not be mourned or buried, but will lie like dung on the ground.” (Jeremiah 16:4) Nobody will mourn them and nobody will bury them. It pays to read it carefully, friends.

The answer is that He has removed His peace from this people. The LORD says, “…for I have removed from this people My peace, My loving devotion, and My compassion…” (Jeremiah 16:5) That's the reason He gives, friends. Notice it's three things taken away, not just one.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “No food will be offered to comfort those who mourn the dead; not even a cup of consolation will be given for the loss of a father or mother.” (Jeremiah 16:7) Bringing food to grieving folks is a kind thing to do, friends. This verse says even that won't happen.

The answer is the sounds of joy and gladness. The LORD says He will remove “…the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom.” (Jeremiah 16:9) He says it will happen “…before your very eyes and in your days…” So Jeremiah's own generation would see it, friends.

The answer is that the people ask what sin they have committed against the LORD. They ask, “What is our iniquity? What is the sin that we have committed against the LORD our God?” (Jeremiah 16:10) They want to know what they did, friends. The LORD already has an answer ready for Jeremiah to give.

The answer is gods. The LORD says their fathers “have forsaken Me… and followed other gods, and served and worshiped them.” (Jeremiah 16:11) They didn't just wander off, friends. They served and worshiped them too.

The answer is stubbornness. The LORD says, “See how each of you follows the stubbornness of his evil heart instead of obeying Me.” (Jeremiah 16:12) The choice is between following their own heart and obeying Him, friends. I know a little about stubborn myself. I once argued with a recipe card, and the recipe card won.
The answer is False. The LORD says they will serve other gods in that land day and night, “…for I will show you no favor.” (Jeremiah 16:13) No favor is promised there, friends. It's a sober line.

The answer is the land of the north and other lands. The LORD says they will say He brought the Israelites up “…out of the land of the north and all the other lands to which He had banished them.” (Jeremiah 16:15) They will no longer say the saying about Egypt (Jeremiah 16:14). They will say this new one instead, friends. Something big is coming for them.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “For I will return them to their land that I gave to their forefathers.” (Jeremiah 16:15) After all that heavy news, friends, here's a promise of coming home. It's the one bright spot in a hard message.

The answer is hunters. The LORD says, “After that I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them down on every mountain and hill, even from the clefts of the rocks.” (Jeremiah 16:16) First fishermen, then hunters, friends. Nowhere to hide, not even in the cracks of the rocks.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “For My eyes are on all their ways. They are not hidden from My face, and their guilt is not concealed from My eyes.” (Jeremiah 16:17) Not some of their ways, friends, but all of them. None of their ways are hidden from Him.

The answer is that He will repay them double for their sin. The LORD says, “And I will first repay them double their iniquity and their sin…” (Jeremiah 16:18) The word “first” matters here, friends. It tells us this is where it starts, and the message isn't finished.

The answer is True. The words to the LORD say, “…the nations will come to You from the ends of the earth…” (Jeremiah 16:19) After all that heavy news, friends, the view widens way out. Now it's nations coming to Him.

The answer is nothing but lies. The nations say, “Our fathers inherited nothing but lies, worthless idols of no benefit at all.” (Jeremiah 16:19) Nothing but lies, friends. That's a clear look back at what they'd been handed.

The answer is “Such are not gods.” The nations ask, “Can man make gods for himself?” and then answer, “Such are not gods!” (Jeremiah 16:20) They don't say lesser or smaller, friends. They say not gods at all.

The answer is that His name is the LORD. The LORD says, “…I will make them know My power and My might; then they will know that My name is the LORD.” (Jeremiah 16:21) The message ends on who He is, friends.
